threads.body: Could we cover this through `ChatAnthropic` instead? The existing `test_chat_anthropic_claude_sonnet_cache_token_details` cassette predates the TTL breakdown. Re-recording it (or adding `"cache_creation": {"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens": 5, "ephemeral_1h_input_tokens": 0}` to its `usage`) makes that test fail on `main` and pass here, with the existing assertions. It also keeps passing on the oldest langchain-anthropic. Then the handler-level cases here wouldn't be needed.

+def test_extract_token_details_anthropic_ttl_breakdown():
+    # Shape produced by langchain-anthropic when Anthropic reports
+    # ``usage.cache_creation`` per cache TTL.
+    usage = {
+        "input_tokens": 22,
+        "output_tokens": 8,
+        "total_tokens": 30,
+        "input_token_details": {
+            "cache_read": 4,
+            "cache_creation": 0,
+            "ephemeral_5m_input_tokens": 5,
+            "ephemeral_1h_input_tokens": 0,
+        },
+    }
+    details = extract_token_details(usage)
+    assert details == {
+        "cache_write_input_tokens": 5,
+        "cache_read_input_tokens": 4,
+    }

replies.body: Sure, I also recorded new cassette, thanks! The test now makes two calls (cache write, then read), since the old prompt was too short to trigger caching.
